name: Russia–NATO
value: Baltic drone alerts 10–11 Nov; no Article 4
summary: Drones crossed Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia on 10–11 Nov; a US soldier at a NATO unit held in UK over Russia spying
state: Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia issued shelter alerts overnight on 10–11 Nov as drones entered from Russia or Belarus; NATO jets tried to down one over northern Lithuania and its origin is still under investigation (Reuters). On 10 Nov UK police arrested a US soldier serving with NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps on suspicion of spying for Russia (Stars and Stripes). No Article 4 request, direct clash or attack on NATO territory was found as of 13 Nov, so the level stays at Watch.
for_you: Air-raid alerts in the Baltic states are short and were lifted within hours. Travellers to the region should follow FCDO travel advice and local authority instructions.
rubric_hit: Watch: drone violations of Baltic airspace 10–11 Nov and a Russia-linked espionage arrest; no Article 4 or clash

sources.title: Reuters via Cyprus Mail — NATO jets scrambled as drone alerts sweep Baltic states
Stars and Stripes — US soldier arrested in Britain, suspected of spying for Russia

why: Direct Russia–NATO confrontation is the most likely path to a European war involving the UK.
drivers: Airspace and drone incursions, sabotage, Baltic incidents, nuclear signalling, Ukraine war spillover.

rubric.alert: Article 4 consultations, a direct military clash, or an attack on NATO territory.
rubric.watch: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.
rubric.normal: No notable incidents on NATO territory in the past two weeks.
